register: MEASURED: TTFT and total seconds, engine-reported prompt and cached tokens, and engine metric deltas, on the deployment stack. CONSTRUCTED: the pressure traffic, the frame count per history and the slice size. COMMITTED: the request bodies (bodies.py), the cache keys (cachekeys.py, D84), the pool sizes and the residency classifier (StudyENG1c).

server_requirement.which: the live2 round-1 32B server, already running; this script starts nothing

caching_statement: Prefix caching is ON for every request. Every measured row carries a `cache` block naming its condition (WARM, COLD, or UNKNOWN BY DESIGN where residency is the measurement), what was cached before it was sent, and whether a repeat could be served from cache. Warm and cold rows are never compared without the comparison saying so. The run tag carries the wall clock, so no run of this script can be served from another run's cache entries.

caveats.touch_wiring: `coordinator._enact` handles KEEP_GPU_WARM by setting `SessionRec.desired_tier` (coordinator.py:482) and emits NO request, so a harness touch cannot move the engine's own eviction order. M2 confirms the ENGINE property the policy's touch lever depends on. It does not confirm that the lever as wired reaches the engine, and must not be cited as if it did.
caveats.warm_ahead_expressibility: `interface.validate_action` accepts a MATERIALIZE only for a session that is already warm or already has a pending question, so warming AHEAD is unexpressible in the committed action space today (reports/study_engine_actions.md section 3). M1 shows the engine pays off a warm-ahead when one is issued; it does not show that an arm can issue one.
caveats.filler_is_text: the pressure traffic is text, not frames. It is a proxy for KV OCCUPANCY and LRU movement only, which is all M2 and M3 ask of it, and is not a proxy for fleet traffic composition.
caveats.m3_trigger_state: the host-resident condition is CREATED here. Across 56 committed 16-device cells the harness's believed_tier is never host, so M3 speaks to the engine action's cost and not to how often the policy would reach it.

question.question: How many items do I have in my hands?
options: A. You have four items in your hands.
B. You are holding exactly one item.
C. There are five items in your hands.
D. You have three items in your hands.
E. You're holding two items in total.
question.source: fleet/data_sources.eval_sessions(), last question of this EVAL session

M1.claim: a warm-ahead prefill of a session's uploaded frames raises the engine's reported cached_tokens for the question that follows

design.warm_arm: one device, 124 frames prefilled ahead of the question as 11-frame prefill-only pieces (engine_actions.WARM_AHEAD_SLICE_TOKENS discipline), then the committed StudyR1 recall body with every frame as a uuid-only reference
design.cold_arm: a different device, the same JPEG files, the same committed recall body, no warm-ahead; D84 gives it its own cache_salt and its own mm uuids so its prefix chain is new to the engine
design.declared_asymmetry: the warm arm's question uploads no image bytes (uuid-only references, the committed StudyRH7 wire form) and the cold arm's uploads all of them, because a uuid the engine has never seen cannot be resolved. Request bytes are recorded per row. The TTFT gap therefore contains avoided upload and vision encode as well as avoided prefill, and must not be read as prefill alone.
design.pass_rule: cached_tokens on the warm arm >= 0.50 * its prompt_tokens (StudyENG1c's own 'gpu' threshold) AND cached_tokens on the cold arm <= 16 (one vLLM block, StudyENG1c's cold gate) AND warm > cold in every rep

frontier.note: frontier_units is the number of one-history units at the YOUNG end of the ladder that still reported reuse. It is measured on this server at this moment and is the only capacity figure M2 relies on.

M3.claim: making a history resident again from the HOST tier is faster than rebuilding it from scratch
M3.trigger_state_note: across 56 committed 16-device cells the coordinator's believed_tier is NEVER host (reports/study_engine_actions.md section 2), so this action's trigger state has never been observed in our harness. This measurement CREATES the host-resident condition on the engine and verifies it; it does not observe the harness reaching it, and must never be cited as if it did.

design.how_host_residency_is_created: build the history, then drive enough other traffic to push it out of the 62944-token GPU pool while staying inside the measured reuse frontier, so the native offload tier (27 GiB = 110592 tokens) still holds it
design.how_it_is_verified: a TWIN history built and pressured identically is probed first, and its residency is classified by StudyENG1c's committed rule over the server's prompt_tokens_by_source / external_prefix_cache counters. The timed reload's OWN counter delta is then classified too, and both must say host or partial_host for the repetition to count.
design.why_a_twin: probing a history reloads it, so the condition cannot be verified on the same object that is then timed. The twin is built immediately after it, from the same frames on its own device salt, and takes the same pressure.

comparators.RELOAD: the host-resident history, full prefix as uuid references, max_tokens 1
comparators.COLD_KV: the SAME uuids under a DIFFERENT cache_salt, so the mm processor cache still holds the frames but the whole KV prefix chain is a new key (D84). This isolates KV reconstruction with no byte upload and no vision re-encode.
comparators.COLD_FULL: a fresh device: new salt, new uuids, every frame's bytes on the wire. This is what the fleet actually pays for a cold rebuild and it is the headline comparator.

design.pass_rule: at least one repetition verified host-resident on BOTH channels, and the median RELOAD time below the median COLD_FULL time. Repetitions that fail verification are DISCARDED and counted, never timed as reloads.

M2.claim: a history whose prefix has been re-read moves DOWN the engine's eviction order, so under pressure that evicts exactly one of two histories it is the untouched one that goes

design.engine_level_touch: a full-prefix, uuid-references-only, max_tokens 1 request, which is StudyENG1c's own touch probe. It uploads no bytes and emits no answer; all it does is read the prefix, which is the only way a client can move vLLM's LRU.
design.conditions: TOUCH builds T then U then touches T, so the recency order youngest-first is (T, U). NOTOUCH builds T then U and touches nothing, so it is (U, T). Both conditions then take the SAME amount of filler traffic and the same probes, so the two predict OPPOSITE winners and a flood that is mis-sized cannot manufacture the asymmetry.
design.flood_rule: (frontier_units - 1) histories' worth of fresh traffic, from the MEASURED frontier, so that exactly one of the two histories falls past it
design.honesty: vLLM cannot pin KV (D150), so this is a probability and not a promise. The result is COUNTS over repetitions. A repetition in which both histories hit or both miss is INDETERMINATE: the pressure missed the one-history window, which is evidence about the sizing and not about the touch.
design.pass_rule: in TOUCH, T hits and U misses in strictly more repetitions than the reverse; AND the NOTOUCH control shows the reverse asymmetry or no asymmetry. If NOTOUCH shows the SAME winner as TOUCH, the touch is not what moved it.

flood_sizing.rule: cross the GPU pool so exactly one of the two histories leaves GPU

superseded.why: at 17 units (190,328 tokens) it evicted BOTH histories to cold in 3 of 3 repetitions, so it was too BIG, not too small; and the probe-measured frontier overstates a passive history's window because probing refreshes what it probes

M2.statistical_note: with 3 decided TOUCH repetitions the strongest available statement is a count; the exact one-sided binomial p against a fair coin is reported beside it and nothing stronger is claimed.
